front: CCAR-P exam format: items, time, passing score?
back: 63 items (multiple-choice + multiple-response) in 120 minutes (~1 min 54 s each). Scaled 720 on 100–1,000. $175. Valid 12 months; free on-time renewal.

front: The seven CCAR-P domains and weights?
back: D1 Solution Design 17% · D2 Models/Prompting/Context 13% · D3 Integration 19% · D4 Evaluation/Testing/Optimization 16% · D5 Governance/Safety/Risk 14% · D6 Stakeholder & Lifecycle 14% · D7 Developer Productivity 7%.

front: The four decisions before building, in order (official prep course)?
back: 1. What work Claude owns (vs. systems vs. humans). 2. What shape the work is (augment, automate, agent). 3. Which reference architecture. 4. Where the work meets Claude (entry point, model, context strategy).

front: Workflow vs. agent: definitions from Building effective agents?
back: Workflow: LLMs and tools orchestrated through predefined code paths. Agent: the LLM dynamically directs its own process and tool use. Start with the simplest solution; add complexity only when needed.

front: The five workflow patterns?
back: Prompt chaining · Routing · Parallelization (sectioning or voting) · Orchestrator-workers · Evaluator-optimizer.

front: Orchestrator-workers vs. prompt chaining vs. evaluator-optimizer?
back: Orchestrator-workers: subtasks can't be predicted until the input is seen. Prompt chaining: fixed, known sequential steps. Evaluator-optimizer: clear criteria exist and iteration measurably improves output.

front: Multi-agent token cost and best fit?
back: Agents ≈ 4× chat tokens; multi-agent ≈ 15×. Fits breadth-first, parallelizable work exceeding one context. Poor fit for tightly coupled work where all agents need the same context (most coding).

front: Do subagents inherit the orchestrator's conversation?
back: No. Pass the task, constraints, and output format explicitly in each delegated task. Scope each subagent's tools.

front: Business value pillars named in the blueprint?
back: Efficiency · Transformation · Productivity · Cost · Performance SLAs. Name the pillar and its metric before designing.

front: Four AI properties as a lens for what Claude should NOT own?
back: Next-token prediction (systems own exact figures) · Knowledge (retrieval/tools own changing facts) · Working memory (systems own state) · Steerability (code owns control flow and hard rules).

front: How to choose a model, per Anthropic?
back: Benchmark on your own eval set ("the most important step"). Efficiency-first (start small, upgrade on gaps) or capability-first (start large, lower effort/downgrade). Compare cost per completed task.

front: Effort vs. switching models?
back: "Tuning effort is often a better lever than switching models." Effort levels: low, medium, high, xhigh, max. Changing top-level effort between requests invalidates the prompt cache.

front: Prompt caching order and breakpoints?
back: Order static → dynamic: tools → system → messages. Exact-prefix match; any upstream change invalidates downstream. Up to 4 breakpoints; minimum 512 tokens on current models. Silent killers: a timestamp or user ID at the top, changed tool definitions, changing effort between requests.

front: Prompt caching TTLs and price multipliers?
back: 5-minute TTL: write 1.25× base input. 1-hour TTL: write 2×. Reads: a small fraction of base input (0.1× on most models, lower on the newest).

front: How do Agent Skills save context?
back: Progressive disclosure: ~100 tokens of name/description per skill always loaded; SKILL.md body loads when relevant; bundled files load only when read; script code never enters context, only its output.

front: Prefill and forced tool_choice on current models?
back: Assistant prefill returns an error on Claude 4.6+; forced tool_choice (any/tool) errors on the newest models. Use structured outputs (JSON schema) or strict tool use for guaranteed shape.

front: Long-document prompt layout?
back: Long documents first (in XML tags), question at the end. Ask for relevant quotes before answering. Improves recall of buried details.

front: Tools for long agent sessions?
back: Context editing (clear stale tool results), compaction (summarize older turns), memory tool (durable facts in files you control), and a structured facts block that survives.

front: Capability bloat: symptoms and fixes?
back: Wrong tool picks and context burned on definitions. Fix: fewer/consolidated tools, scoped sub-agents, tool search with defer_loading, and remove tools the role never uses.

front: Official Sample 1 rule: least privilege?
back: Remove capabilities the role doesn't need. Logging (detective) and confirmations (compensating) are weaker; a bigger model doesn't change authorization scope.

front: MCP token passthrough: why forbidden?
back: The server forwards a client token it didn't validate for itself: breaks audience validation and enables confused-deputy attacks. Validate tokens issued for the server; use its own scoped downstream credentials.

front: Identity in agent tool calls: where must it come from?
back: From authentication (SSO/session), with per-user delegated tokens and server-side authorization. Never from text the model read or wrote.

front: Refusals on current models: how do they arrive?
back: HTTP 200 with stop_reason "refusal". Error-rate dashboards miss them. Instrument refusals separately and configure fallback per request.

front: 429 vs. 529 vs. spend-cap 429?
back: 429 rate limit: honor retry-after, ramp gradually. 529: API overloaded, retry with backoff or fall back. Spend-cap 429: no retry-after; retries keep failing, so alert instead.

front: Contextual Retrieval numbers, and when to skip RAG?
back: Skip RAG under ~200k tokens (~500 pages): full KB in the prompt with caching. Otherwise prepend 50–100 tokens of chunk context before embedding and BM25: failures fall 35% (contextual embeddings), 49% (+ contextual BM25), 67% (+ reranking).

front: Retrieval for part numbers, error codes, IDs?
back: Keyword/BM25 in a hybrid setup plus exact-match filters, then rerank. Embeddings blur near-identical identifiers.

front: Retrieval for live state and for aggregates?
back: Live state (order status, balance): a tool call to the system of record. Aggregates (totals by region): a read-only query tool. Not vector search.

front: API/CLI vs. MCP vs. agent-to-agent?
back: API/CLI: one consumer, deterministic call. MCP: one integration reused by many Claude clients (tools, resources, prompts). A2A: independent agents, often cross-org, each owning tools, state, policy.

front: Progressive discovery vs. monolithic context?
back: Monolithic: small, static, always-needed context (cache it). Progressive: large catalogs with sparse use per task (tool search, Skills, retrieval). Trade-off: round trips vs. bloat.

front: Bedrock / Vertex vs. direct Claude API?
back: Cloud routes fit procurement, residency, and FedRAMP needs but lag on some features (e.g., Files API, Skills, MCP connector) and set their own deprecation dates. Constraints rule routes out before latency/cost.

front: Evaluation metric dimensions in the blueprint?
back: Accuracy · Latency · Cost · Safety · Security. Criteria must be specific, measurable, achievable, relevant.

front: Grading methods in Anthropic's order of preference?
back: Code-based (fastest, most reliable) → LLM-based (validate against humans first, then scale) → human (gold standard; avoid at scale). Prioritize volume over hand-graded quality.

front: LLM-as-judge essentials?
back: Detailed rubric, constrained output (score/label), reasoning before scoring, a different prompt (ideally stronger model) than the system under test, and agreement checked against human labels.

front: pass@k vs. pass^k?
back: pass@k: at least one success in k tries. pass^k: all k succeed (75% per trial over 3 trials ≈ 42%). Customer-facing agents need pass^k thinking.

front: A/B testing a prompt change correctly?
back: Hypothesis, one variable, primary + guardrail metrics, sample size estimated up front, report effect size and uncertainty. Run offline evals before online tests.

front: Official Sample 3: wrong answers after a document refresh, model unchanged?
back: Investigate retrieval/indexing first (stale or broken index, mismatched embeddings). Temperature, weights, and window size are wrong triggers.

front: Quality drops after switching to a smaller model, only on one category?
back: Model mismatch on hard cases: route that category to the larger model, keep the small one for the rest, verify on evals.

front: Message Batches API facts?
back: 50% off input and output; asynchronous (most finish < 1 h, expire at 24 h); up to 100,000 requests or 256 MB; not ZDR-eligible; wrong for user-facing latency.

front: The right unit for cost optimization?
back: Cost per successfully completed task, including retries and human rework. Not price per token.

front: What to log per request in production?
back: Request ID, model, prompt version, tokens incl. cache reads/writes, latency, stop_reason, tool calls with args and results, retrieved chunk IDs. Redact PII. Trace across agent steps.

front: What the model's training reduces vs. what the app must enforce?
back: Training reduces harmful content and many jailbreaks. The application must enforce business rules, authorization, grounding, and PII policy. Claude can't enforce a rule it was never given.

front: The safety stack along the request path?
back: Input screening → system prompt (guidance) → tool-call authorization (deterministic) → output screening → audit logs. Each layer catches the previous one's blind spot.

front: Model-based vs. deterministic checks?
back: Deterministic (regex, allowlists, schema, permission lookups) for exact rules: cheap, predictable, auditable. Model-based (classifiers, judges) for fuzzy semantics: probabilistic, need evals. Combine.

front: Fail closed vs. fail open?
back: When a control errors or times out, fail closed for consequential actions (block or route to a human). Failing open lets unchecked requests through.

front: Strongest defense against indirect prompt injection?
back: Limit what a hijacked agent can do (least privilege, no exfiltration paths, approvals), plus keep untrusted content in tool_result blocks and screen tool outputs. Detection alone is probabilistic.

front: Human-in-the-loop routing dimensions?
back: Confidence (calibrated on labeled data, not self-reported), reversibility, and cost of a wrong answer. Automate + sample the low-risk; require human approval for irreversible or high-cost.

front: HIPAA on the Claude API?
back: BAA required before PHI. HIPAA readiness is enabled in the Console and is permanent; ineligible features error. Managed Agents and Claude Code are not covered. No PHI in JSON schemas.

front: FedRAMP High routes for Claude?
back: Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (also DoD IL4/IL5) and Google Cloud Vertex AI.

front: Compliance mapping pattern (official prep course)?
back: Map each obligation to a named control, an owner, and an evidence artifact so the architecture can be audited.

front: Is a model fair after removing protected attributes?
back: Not proven. Proxies remain (zip code, school, name). Measure outcomes by group on varied eval data and monitor production rates.

front: Discovery: what to capture first?
back: Current process and baseline, volume and peaks, latency tolerance, cost of a wrong answer and reversibility, data location/sensitivity, regulatory and procurement constraints, success metric. Document assumptions.

front: Presenting a trade-off to executives?
back: Pair each option with cost, risk, and what a reversal would take; give a recommendation and what would change your mind. Record it in an ADR.

front: A good SLA for an LLM system?
back: Measured thresholds (p95 latency, quality floor on sampled review, availability), a fallback, and a defined breach response. Never "always correct."

front: Iterate vs. re-architect?
back: Iterate when the failure is local (a prompt, retrieval for one category). Re-architect when it is structural (wrong pattern, data outgrew the store, volume outgrew the design).

front: Model deprecation response?
back: At least 60 days' notice. Treat as a review trigger: eval the successor, re-baseline cost/latency, fix regressions, migrate before retirement. Bedrock/Google set their own dates.

front: Handoff package that survives the architect leaving?
back: Architecture and data-flow diagrams, ADRs, prompt/config registry, eval suite with thresholds and run instructions, runbooks (symptom → action → owner), named owners.

front: Claude Code settings precedence?
back: Managed → command-line → .claude/settings.local.json → .claude/settings.json → ~/.claude/settings.json. Permission rules evaluate deny → ask → allow.

front: CLAUDE.md vs. hooks vs. permissions vs. managed settings?
back: CLAUDE.md is guidance. Permissions and hooks are enforcement (hook exit code 2 blocks). Managed settings enforce org-wide with no opt-out.

front: Where do team conventions, personal overrides, and security policy go?
back: Team: project CLAUDE.md / .claude/settings.json (committed). Personal: settings.local.json or user files. Security policy: managed settings.

front: Claude Code in CI?
back: Headless mode: claude -p with --output-format json and a scoped tool allowlist, usually via the GitHub Action. Humans still approve merges; use an independent reviewer, not the authoring session.
